displayedOrder.name: Mistlight Conservatory
displayedOrder.prompt:
Create realistic, production-quality UI designs with clear hierarchy, strong typography, intentional imagery, and purposeful spacing.
Use case: ui-mockup, an aspirational art-direction concept for a real Three.js/WebGL educational 3D adventure for Chinese grade 9 English, Unit 13 environmental protection. Direction name: Mistlight Conservatory. This is a SINGLE focused primary screen, not a feature inventory. Target dimensions 1536 x 1024 landscape desktop. Full bleed app, no browser or device frame, no multi-panel collage, no concept labels. Current date anchor 2026-11-06, do not display a date.
Attached Image 1 is the user's original source image: preserve the grounded garden valley, graceful central curved glass conservatory with side wings and entrance rotunda, treehouse behind on left, timber workshop left foreground, loop cobblestone paths around a circular flowerbed, pond and little wooden bridge front right, layered misty hills. Image 2 is the prior draft, a secondary composition guide, not the final quality ceiling. Render a much more carefully crafted game-quality environment with physically believable PBR materials and exquisite geometry, not crude low-poly primitives. Preserve miniature scale and near-orthographic 45-degree overhead camera, restrained sage, moss and ivory palette.
Art direction: fine slender dark metal greenhouse beams with believable joints, subtly aged transparent glass reflecting sky and transmitting light, plants visible inside, wood grain and end-grain, bevelled cobblestone with damp edges and moss in crevices, individual roof shingles and railings, natural clustered leaves with translucency, detailed reeds and pond bank. Soft early morning light after rain, delicate contact shadows, believable ambient occlusion, selective damp specular highlights, atmospheric depth. Calm mature premium 3D game, NOT toy plastic, no neon, no floating island, no giant mushrooms, no fantasy magic. Environment occupies at least 85% of frame. Everything is readable in focus, no excessive depth blur.
Narrative state: initial investigation. A narrow stream flows from exposed planting beds near greenhouse on the right midground down to the pond; a subtle brown sediment plume enters the pond, not toxic bright green sludge. A couple of discarded bottles near the bank are a separate observation. Garden otherwise beautiful and welcoming, not fully restored and not devastated.
UI: tasteful elegant dark green Cormorant-like serif masthead in sky at upper left exact text 'THE ENGLISH VALLEY', smaller sans text 'UNIT 13 · A VALLEY WORTH PROTECTING'. Compact four-season selector beneath masthead 'SPRING   SUMMER   AUTUMN   WINTER'. Top right a restrained day/sound control. Only TWO world-attached cream/moss labels near real objects: 'Cloudy water' at sediment plume, 'Talk to the gardener' near an extremely small distant neutral gardener at greenhouse. Keep these readable, not huge overlay badges.
Bottom left a small well-spaced warm ivory mission slip, about 26% viewport width, exact text 'Why is the stream cloudy after rain?' then small supporting line 'Look closely. Ask questions. Follow the evidence.' and one dark green primary button 'Explore the stream'. Bottom right a slim quiet navigation 'MAP   FIELD JOURNAL'. No five skill rooms, scores, percentage progress, clue count, XP or dense dashboard. UI body 18-20px equivalent, concise sans-serif. Produce a single beautiful plausible high-end realtime 3D game screenshot-like CONCEPT IMAGE, visual target only, not an actual implemented screenshot.

displayedOrder.name: Along the Living Stream
displayedOrder.prompt:
Create realistic, production-quality UI designs with clear hierarchy, strong typography, intentional imagery, and purposeful spacing.
Use case: ui-mockup, one focused playable-scene art-direction CONCEPT, not actual software. A mature grade 9 English environmental investigation game built later with real Three.js/WebGL. Direction name: Along the Living Stream. Target dimensions 1536 x 1024 desktop landscape, no device/browser frame, no collage, no design-option labels. Date anchor 2026-11-06, do not show date.
Attached image 1 is the user's garden valley source and image 2 the earlier overview concept. Keep the same geographical world and key building identity, but explore it at human scale rather than as an overhead map. The great curved metal-and-glass conservatory with side wings must remain recognizable in the middle distance, a timber treehouse to its back left, a wooden workshop along a winding cobblestone trail, a small wooden bridge crossing the foreground stream, and layered mountains beyond. Restrained sage green and weathered timber identity carried from reference, richer natural colours without neon. It is an inland garden valley, not Alba's Spanish island. Do not copy any game character.
Camera: intimate third-person over-the-shoulder exploration at a student's height, around 1.4m, lens equivalent 35mm, broad beautiful perspective, carefully composed stream in foreground leading eye toward conservatory. A small age-15 student explorer with a plain forest-green rain jacket, neutral dark trousers and a modest canvas field bag occupies only lower-left 12% of image, seen from behind, no childish proportions, no face closeup. They hold an understated field camera/notebook and look toward the stream. A gardener is barely visible farther along greenhouse path. The world is luminous and inviting.
Art quality: sophisticated stylized naturalism with believable high-quality PBR 3D game rendering, softly rounded architecture edges, water with physically plausible reflections and visible shallow stones, damp timber end grain, chipped limestone, clustered foliage with thin leaf translucency, ferns, reeds, patches of moss. Warm sun emerging after rain, soft directional shadows, light haze at distant mountain ridge. Crisp near surfaces, subtle distant atmosphere. Not crude low-poly, not flat illustration, not a photograph, not hyper-sharp grunge or oversaturated cartoon.
Story evidence: foreground stream has a localized muted earth-brown plume where a little runoff channel from bare soil meets it; clearer upstream water visible beyond. A few separately placed discarded bottles at bank. This is an investigable problem, not a giant pollution disaster; no dead animals. The cause is a hypothesis to investigate, not text already giving the answer.
UI minimal and readable with two fonts max: top left small Cormorant-like masthead 'THE ENGLISH VALLEY' and understated 'UNIT 13 · FIELD VISIT'. Beneath it a small quiet mission line 'Why is the stream cloudy after rain?'. Near the stream a tiny unobtrusive physical hotspot ring and label 'Inspect the stream'. Lower-right an elegant compact warm-ivory field-note panel around 25% viewport width: heading 'FIELD NOTE', one observation 'The water looks different here.', a prompt 'What could explain the change?', and a single dark evergreen primary button 'Record an observation'. Bottom center only slim tools 'LOOK   ASK   JOURNAL', high-contrast but restrained. At upper right a tiny 'MAP' control. Do not add quest lists, scores, XP, clue counters, big dialogue bubbles or multiple panels. One main action: noticing and recording evidence. Environmental view occupies at least 80%. Clean plausible screen hierarchy and generous breathing space; text readable at 18-20px equivalent. A beautiful premium indie 3D adventure visualization with English as an observation tool.

displayedOrder.name: Rainworks Valley
displayedOrder.prompt:
Create realistic, production-quality UI designs with clear hierarchy, strong typography, intentional imagery, and purposeful spacing.
Use case: ui-mockup, a single premium playable-scene CONCEPT for THE ENGLISH VALLEY, grade 9 English environmental inquiry in a real 3D WebGL game world to be built later. Direction name: Rainworks Valley. Target dimensions 1536 x 1024 desktop landscape. Full-bleed app content, no browser/device frame, no collage, no option label. Current date anchor 2026-11-06; no visible date.
Image 1 is the original garden valley reference. Image 2 is a prior overview draft. Preserve the same recognizable curved glass greenhouse, side wings, timber workshop on left, treehouse in rear, cobbled paths and little bridge near a pond. Reinterpret with deeply refined physically believable rendered materials and a closer three-quarter overhead GAME CAMERA centred on an interactive streamside restoration site, like an exquisitely crafted environmental simulation rather than a flat map. The ground continues naturally into misty wooded valley hills; no floating island, no hex grid. Retain the reference's muted sage, deep moss, warm weathered timber and warm ivory, with richer wet earth and subtle water highlights.
Frame composition: greenhouse and treehouse in upper middle background with real internal planting beds visible through faint reflections. A small timber workshop upper left has cut wood, reused flowerboxes, rain barrel and natural hand tools. Foreground and middle-right show a winding stream, a beautiful small bridge, an exposed patch of muddy soil that drains toward the stream, and a narrow bank suitable for a planted buffer. There is realistic height variation in ground, rivulets, pebbles and banks. A modest trail of sediment runs from bare soil to the water after rainfall, while upstream looks clearer. Mature inviting natural environment, not a devastated wasteland.
Interaction state: the student is testing a proposed measure. Show one very subtle translucent sage outline of an UNPLACED planting strip along a short section of bank; next to it a few actual plant plugs in reusable trays and a realistic small trowel. The outline is a clearly prospective placement preview, not neon magic. A faint dotted placement boundary is enough, no giant arrows or sci-fi effects. No real person or floating hands needed. Do not portray the whole river instantly cured.
Rendering art direction: meticulous game-quality 3D geometry, beveled weathered wood planks, screws, rough limestone with moss, realistic shallow water with restrained reflections, smooth but detailed foliage clusters, fine metal joinery and slightly rain-spotted greenhouse glass, discreet plant scatter on banks. Dramatic yet gentle overcast light after rain with a warm break of sunlight, coherent ambient occlusion and soft contact shadows, selective wet-surface highlights. Not blocky primitives, not plastic toys, not flat vector, no futuristic equipment. A realistic handcrafted environmental puzzle world.
UI: small restrained elegant serif title at upper left 'THE ENGLISH VALLEY', secondary sans text 'UNIT 13 · TEST YOUR PLAN'. Upper right tiny 'MAP' and quiet sound control. Lower-left a shallow cream workbench strip with only three beautifully spaced object choices represented by actual rendered objects plus short text 'Plants', 'Reused wood', 'Rain barrel'; 'Plants' selected. Lower-right one compact warm-ivory action panel with heading 'Try a planted buffer', small sentence 'Will less soil reach the stream?', single dark evergreen button 'Test the next rainfall', and understated text 'A simplified model'. The primary action is compare-and-test, not win or submit quiz. No numerical ecological score, no unverified chemistry readout, no percent completion, no XP, no dashboards, no five skill tabs. Text comfortably readable at 18-20px equivalent, max two fonts. World remains at least 80% of image, with generous clear space and a visual route for runoff easy to follow. This is one polished aspirational screen conveying hands-on reasoning and the pleasure of a believable small 3D world.

spatialRule: Option 1 determines world layout. Options 2/3 must be re-framed inside that same geometry; no moved workshop, duplicated bridge or independent terrain.
